title: Titanic evidence-led April 14 ice warnings
visual_director_notes: Hand-selected, fixed scene order. The only surviving period ice warning photos are archival documents; no fictional footage of the collision, no copyright-restricted museum picture.

source_candidates.risk: Do not say this is Caronia or Baltic's distinct message
The exact memo reports several sightings, but not a modern satellite map
This is after the collision and is NOT a pre-collision ice warning

source_candidates.file: Lightoller and Murdoch, last photo on Titanic.webp
source_candidates.risk: Identity and date from exact item metadata, no bridge collision scene
Cannot prove pictured berg is the one struck; old LOC caption details unverified

shots.onscreen_label: SS AMERIKA ICE WARNING • RELAYED VIA TITANIC, 14 APRIL
shots.editorial_why: Actual 14 April 1912 message excerpt reports ice; exact date and source document are relevant to narrated warning claims.

shots.onscreen_label: U.S. NAVY REPORT: APRIL 14 ICE SIGHTINGS
shots.editorial_why: Actual contemporary Navy hydrographer memorandum establishes 1912 reported ice positions; no modern digital-map fabrication.

shots.onscreen_label: CARONIA MESSAGE, 9:00 AM — BRITISH INQUIRY
shots.editorial_why: The available original Amerika memorandum is NOT the Caronia message. Use an honest source-referenced text-and-time graphic, not an incorrectly labelled photograph.

shots.onscreen_label: BALTIC RELAY, 1:42 PM — BRITISH INQUIRY
shots.editorial_why: No verified freely reusable image of that exact Baltic communication; precise labelled period report summary is necessary.

shots.onscreen_label: THE ACTUAL TITANIC BEFORE THE COLLISION
shots.editorial_why: A genuine pre-14 April ship view anchors the speed question without falsely showing the ship navigating at night.

shots.onscreen_label: ICE REGION AND THE SHIP'S NAVIGATION — SCHEMATIC
shots.editorial_why: Historical route and uncertainty need a source-labelled original graphic, not a falsely exact satellite map.

shots.onscreen_label: 1912 BERG IMAGE, REPORTED FROM CARPATHIA — IDENTITY UNCERTAIN
shots.editorial_why: Actual circa-1912 photo titled iceberg from Carpathia; source does not prove it was the iceberg Titanic struck. Show as illustrative period evidence only.

shots.onscreen_label: DARK HORIZON: VISIBILITY EXPLAINED
shots.editorial_why: No photograph of Titanic's precise moonless view exists. Clearly labelled original schematic shows visual contrast challenge.

shots.onscreen_label: LIGHTOLLER AND MURDOCH • TITANIC, APRIL 1912
shots.editorial_why: Real dated pre-sinking Titanic officer photograph illustrates actual lookout command context, not the fatal lookout moment.

shots.onscreen_label: LOOKOUT LINE OF SIGHT — EXPLANATORY MODEL
shots.editorial_why: Technical visibility geometry is best explained by sourced diagram; no authentic photo captures lookout line of sight at impact.

shots.onscreen_label: REAL TITANIC WIRELESS SIGNAL • 15 APRIL 1912
shots.editorial_why: Authentic signal preserved by UK National Archives indicates real communications technology; clearly labelled post-collision, not an ice-warning telegram.

shots.onscreen_label: WIRELESS MYTHS VS DOCUMENTED RECORD
shots.editorial_why: Original evidence comparison diagram avoids fabricating a commercial-message record.

shots.onscreen_label: ICE FIELDS ARE REGIONS, NOT A PRECISE COLLISION TARGET
shots.editorial_why: Revisit actual 14 April coordinates from period telegram to distinguish field sightings from the exact later striking berg.

shots.onscreen_label: ICE REPORT AREAS, NOT EXACT ICEBERG LOCATIONS
shots.editorial_why: Reconstructed map must clearly show imperfect 1912 coordinates rather than invented satellite precision.

shots.onscreen_label: CAPTAIN EDWARD J. SMITH, BEFORE THE VOYAGE
shots.editorial_why: Genuine portrait of actual commander contextualizes later scrutiny of speed and warnings; do not assert it was taken on the bridge that night.

shots.onscreen_label: THE LIMITS OF EVENING NAVIGATION
shots.editorial_why: Only a schematic can explain source certainty and navigation choices without pretending a camera was aboard.

shots.onscreen_label: TITANIC UNDER WAY BEFORE THE NORTH ATLANTIC
shots.editorial_why: Authentic original April 1912 vessel photo, deliberately labelled pre-disaster, supports temporal transition from day into night.

shots.onscreen_label: THE 14 APRIL WARNING RECORD REMAINED
shots.editorial_why: A separate close reading of the exact contemporaneous memo reinforces source-based chronology, not generic filler.

shots.onscreen_label: PERIOD ICEBERG PHOTO — NOT CONFIRMED FATAL BERG
shots.editorial_why: The photographed period iceberg illustrates a real type of hazard, paired with the actual pre-collision warning; never present as exact collision evidence.

shots.onscreen_label: 11:40 PM — THE ICE WARNING REACHED THE BRIDGE
shots.editorial_why: A labelled time card avoids invented moving shots of the moment of impact.

editorial_note_count_correction: A source-by-source recount confirmed eleven archive photographs/documents; film picture bytes are unchanged. Prior report said ten.
